collections.title: Amidah: praise, petition, and thanks
collections.connection: Continue in the six-session Tefillah course.

lines.hebrew: ברוך אתה ה׳ אלהינו ואלהי אבותינו
lines.translation: Blessed are You, Lord our God and God of our ancestors.
lines.note: Direct address and inherited communal language establish the blessing.
answers: Blessed are You, Lord our God and God of our ancestors.
Heal us, Lord, and we shall be healed.
lines.feedback: Right. Direct address and inherited names open the blessing.

lines.translation: Heal us, Lord, and we shall be healed.
lines.note: A petition names a need without becoming a legal or medical directive.
answers: Blessed are You, Lord our God and God of our ancestors.
Heal us, Lord, and we shall be healed.
lines.feedback: Right. This is a petition, not a ruling or a diagnosis.

lines.note: The plural voice makes gratitude communal as well as personal.
answers: Heal us, Lord, and we shall be healed.
Blessed are You, Lord our God and God of our ancestors.
lines.feedback: Right. The plural voice makes the thanks communal.

collections.title: Exile, Babylonia, and community
collections.connection: Continue in the History and Wider World course.

lines.translation: Seek the welfare of the city.
lines.note: Ask who hears the command and in what setting before applying it.
answers: Seek the welfare of the city.
For in its welfare you will have welfare.
lines.feedback: Right. Name who is addressed, and in what city, before applying it.

lines.translation: For in its welfare you will have welfare.
lines.note: The source links the community’s wellbeing to the city in which it lives.
answers: Seek the welfare of the city.
For in its welfare you will have welfare.
lines.feedback: Right. The community’s welfare is tied to the city’s.

lines.note: Place, language, and institutions shape the questions communities face.
answers: Seek the welfare of the city.
For in its welfare you will have welfare.
lines.feedback: Right. Place and institutions shape the questions that follow.
